To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

m-calpain, the most thoroughly characterized member of the Ca2+-dependent calpain family of proteases, is a heterodimer of a 79-kDa large subunit and a 29-kDa small subunit, that both subunits are cysteine protease domains, that the small subunit contains the active site cysteine and the Ca2+-binding site, and that the large subunit contains the Ca2+-induced calpain activation site.

m-calpain, the major calpain isoform found in muscle, crystallizes in space group P1 with cell dimensions of a = 85.1, b = 86.5, c = 90.4 A, and in space group P2(1), with a = 85, b = 90, c = 85.8 A, beta = 95.8 degrees.

the structure of m-calpain has been determined to 2.5 A resolution, that the structure reveals that the catalytic site of calpains is a cysteine protease, and that a new type of Ca(2+)-binding site, which is not a conventional EF-hand site, has been identified.
